method: Melt chocolate and butter together and cool slightly. Whisk in sugar and eggs for 1-2 minutes for a crinkly top, then fold in flour and cocoa gently. Bake until the edges are set and the centre is slightly soft.
Whisk melted butter, sugar and eggs, then fold in cocoa and flour gently until just combined. Bake until a toothpick shows moist crumbs.
Fold the flour and baking powder in gently; stop as soon as no dry flour is visible.
Whisk sugar and eggs well for a shiny crust, then fold in the flour. Do not overbake.
Whisk oil, sugar and eggs, then fold in the dry ingredients with a spatula.
Cream butter and sugar 3-5 minutes until pale, add the eggs gradually, then fold in flour and baking powder and loosen with milk.
Cream butter and sugar 3-5 minutes until pale, add eggs one at a time, then fold in flour and milk alternately.
Use room-temperature ingredients, cream butter and sugar well and add the eggs slowly.
Whisk eggs and sugar until thick, add oil and milk, then fold in sifted flour and baking powder.
Mix wet and dry ingredients separately and combine until just mixed; the batter is thin.
Whisk wet and dry separately, combine with a few strokes and fold in the blueberries; lumps are fine.
Cream butter and sugar, add flour and milk alternately, fill liners two thirds full.
Muffin method: mix wet and dry separately and combine with a few strokes; lumps are fine.
Whisk wet and dry separately, then combine gently; do not overmix.
Stir wet into dry with a spatula until just combined.
Cream butter with both sugars, add the egg, fold in the dry ingredients and chips, chill 30 minutes and bake until the edges are golden and the centres look slightly soft.
Cream butter and sugar, chill the dough 30-60 minutes and bake on a cool tray.
Do not over-cream; chill the dough before rolling or scooping.
Mix just until combined and chill the scooped dough before baking.
Use softened (not melted) butter and chill the dough for 30 minutes.
Mix and knead about 10 minutes, proof until doubled, shape, proof again and bake until it sounds hollow when tapped.
Knead until the dough passes the windowpane test, proof until doubled, bake until it sounds hollow.
Knead well, proof until doubled, shape and proof again before baking.
Use a wet dough, fold rather than knead, and bake hot with steam.
Mash 3 ripe bananas and stir the wet mix into the dry with only a few strokes.
Mash 3 ripe bananas, whisk with oil and eggs, then fold into the dry ingredients gently.
Rub cold butter into the flour, bring together gently without kneading and bake hot.
Use cold cream or butter, handle the dough as little as possible and do not twist the cutter.
Rub in cold butter, add liquid in one go and pat out; do not knead.
Rub cold butter into the flour and sugar, press into a tin, chill, prick with a fork and bake low and slow until pale golden.
Do not overwork the dough; chill before baking at a low temperature.
